subject.title: [Feature]: Invoke tools directly without LLM round-trip

question: Which remaining direct-invoke surfaces should OpenClaw core support beyond the shipped HTTP/RPC/SDK, command-cron, and skill slash-command paths, and what owner/security gates are required for host filesystem, exec/session, generic slash-command, and CLI access?
rationale: The unresolved scope can expose process, filesystem, session, cron, Gateway, and node actions without a model turn, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent product boundary or security gate shape.

options.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow slices
options.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing active host-filesystem and readiness PRs, requiring owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and live proof before merge.

options.title: Limit support to shipped paths
options.body: Declare HTTP/RPC/SDK, command cron, and skill tool-dispatch slash commands sufficient for now, and reject broader host-FS, exec, generic slash-command, and CLI dispatch until a sponsored proposal exists.

options.title: Approve broader direct execution
options.body: Allow broader direct tool execution only with a named security design, upgrade proof, and operator-facing controls that make the risk explicit.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and land narrow slices
recommendation.body: Leave this issue open while reviewing active host-filesystem and readiness PRs, requiring owner gates, safe defaults, docs, audit coverage, and live proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history around dangerous-tool lists, shared-secret HTTP tool-invoke auth, and operator-boundary documentation makes steipete the best available owner for the security/product boundary decision.
